name: ct
description: Generic container types: Vec, Map, Set, Queue, Deque and Pair.  A container is created with a struct literal whose fields are all zero or null; there is no constructor function, and the first insertion allocates. A method that changes a container returns it, and that result must be captured (`v 10 push! -> v`). Call `release` on a Vec, Map, Set, Queue or Deque when done to free its memory.  Example:   use ct    fn main() {   	ct::Vec<i64> { data = null len = 0 cap = 0 } -> v   	v 10 push! -> v   	v 20 push! -> v   	v 0 get! print nl                       // 10   	v release    	ct::Map<i64> { keys = null values = null states = null len = 0 cap = 0 } -> m   	m "alice" 42 insert! -> m   	m "alice" get! print nl                 // 42   	m release    	ct::Set { keys = null states = null len = 0 cap = 0 } -> s   	s "alice" add! -> s   	s "alice" contains print nl             // 1   	s release    	ct::Queue<i64> { data = null head = 0 tail = 0 len = 0 cap = 0 } -> q   	q 1 enqueue! -> q   	q 2 enqueue! -> q   	q dequeue! -> q -> first   	first print nl                          // 1   	q release    	ct::Deque<i64> { data = null head = 0 tail = 0 len = 0 cap = 0 } -> d   	d 1 push_back! -> d   	d 0 push_front! -> d   	d peek_front! print nl                  // 0   	d release    	ct::Pair<i64, str> { first = 42 second = "hello" } -> p   	p unpack -> b -> a   	a print " " print b print nl            // 42 hello   }

structs.name: Deque
structs.description: Double-ended queue with elements of type T.

structs.name: Map
structs.description: Hash map with string keys and values of any type V -- i64, f64, str, ptr or a struct. A value lives in a tagged slot (mem::set_any), so it reads back as what was inserted, and the map holds a reference to a string or a struct for as long as the entry is in it.

fields.name: first
fields.description: The first element of type T

fields.name: second
fields.description: The second element of type U

structs.name: Queue
structs.description: FIFO Queue with elements of type T.

fields.name: len
fields.description: Current number of elements (0 to cap)

functions.name: add
functions.description: Add an element to the set. If the element already exists, the set is unchanged. Returns the updated set which must be captured.
examples: s "alice" add! -> s  // re-bind the returned set

functions.name: capacity
functions.description: Get the allocated capacity. Capacity is always >= length. The vector can hold up to 'capacity' elements before needing to reallocate.

functions.name: contains
functions.description: Check if an element exists in the set.

functions.name: dequeue
functions.description: Remove and return the front element. Returns error if queue is empty. Returns the value and updated queue.
examples: q dequeue! -> q -> val  // the queue is on top, the element under it

functions.name: enqueue
functions.description: Add an element to the back of the queue. Returns the updated queue which must be captured.
examples: q 42 enqueue! -> q  // re-bind the returned queue

functions.name: first
functions.description: Get the first element of a pair.

functions.name: get
functions.description: Get the value for a key. Returns an error if the key is not found.

functions.name: get
functions.description: Get element at index. Panics if index is out of bounds (< 0 or >= len).

functions.name: has
functions.description: Check if a key exists in the map.

functions.name: insert
functions.description: Insert a key-value pair into the map. If the key already exists, the value is updated. Returns the updated map which must be captured.
examples: m "alice" 42 insert! -> m  // re-bind the returned map

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the deque is empty.

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the map is empty.

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the queue is empty.

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the set is empty.

functions.name: is_empty
functions.description: Check if the vector is empty (length == 0).

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of entries in the map.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the queue.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the set.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get the number of elements in the vector.

functions.name: peek_back
functions.description: View the back element without removing it.

functions.name: peek_front
functions.description: View the front element without removing it.

functions.name: peek
functions.description: View the front element without removing it. Returns error if queue is empty.

functions.name: pop_back
functions.description: Remove and return the back element.
examples: d pop_back! -> d -> val  // the deque is on top, the element under it

functions.name: pop_front
functions.description: Remove and return the front element.
examples: d pop_front! -> d -> val  // the deque is on top, the element under it

functions.name: pop
functions.description: Pop and return the last element. Panics if the vector is empty. Returns both the element and the updated vector.
examples: v pop! -> v -> elem  // the vector is on top, the element under it

functions.name: push_back
functions.description: Push an element to the back.
examples: d 42 push_back! -> d  // re-bind the returned deque

functions.name: push_front
functions.description: Push an element to the front.
examples: d 42 push_front! -> d  // re-bind the returned deque

functions.name: push
functions.description: Push an element to the end of the vector. Automatically grows capacity when full (doubles size, starting at 8). Returns the updated vector which must be captured.
examples: v 42 push! -> v  // re-bind the returned vector

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the deque's memory.

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the map's memory. IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a map to prevent memory leaks. After calling release, the map should not be used.

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the queue's memory.

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the set's memory. IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a set to prevent memory leaks.

functions.name: release
functions.description: Free the vector's memory. IMPORTANT: Always call this when done with a vector to prevent memory leaks. After calling release, the vector should not be used.

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Remove a key from the map. Returns error if the key is not found. Returns the updated map which must be captured.
examples: m "alice" remove! -> m  // re-bind the returned map

functions.name: remove
functions.description: Remove an element from the set. Returns error if the element is not found. Returns the updated set which must be captured.
examples: s "alice" remove! -> s  // re-bind the returned set

functions.name: reset
functions.description: Remove all elements, keeping allocated capacity. Useful for reusing a vector without reallocating.
examples: v reset -> v  // re-bind the returned vector

functions.name: second
functions.description: Get the second element of a pair.

functions.name: set
functions.description: Set element at index. Panics if index is out of bounds (< 0 or >= len). Returns the updated vector which must be captured.
examples: v 0 100 set! -> v  // re-bind the returned vector

functions.name: unpack
functions.description: Unpack a pair onto the stack. Returns both elements: first is deeper, second on top.
examples: p unpack -> b -> a  // second on top, so it binds first
